notes:
Search and fetch limits cut this research short. I read the full Enduring Word (Guzik) and Precept Austin pages, but both came back cut off part way through. For everything else I only have search snippets (Gill, Ellicott, Calvin, Matthew Henry, the Pulpit Commentary and others on StudyLight and Bible Hub, plus Ligonier, Monergism, TGC, bible.org and GotQuestions). I found nothing from the Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Bible Odyssey or prosperity/word-of-faith sources, so those are left out as you asked. Notes without a citation tag come from the two full pages and carry their URL.

**v. 1**
- Precept Austin says chapter 2 zooms in on Day 6. It reads "completed" as ruling out theistic evolution. It also cites Victor Hamilton: the universe is no longer being created, though creatures still reproduce. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Ryrie (quoted there) says "hosts" probably means everything God made, not just stars or angels. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Henry Morris, also quoted there: the emphasis on completion refutes evolutionary pantheism and materialism; creation is complete, not continuing. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62647/

**vv. 2–3**
- Traditional reading: God did not rest because He was tired. He rested to show His creating work was done, to set the seven-day week, and to model the blessing of rest. The seventh day has no "evening and morning" phrase, which Guzik takes as a sign that God's rest points to an eternal rest in Christ (Heb 4:9–11). https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- The ESV Study Bible note (quoted by Precept Austin) ties divine rest to ancient Near Eastern temple-building. On this reading the earth is meant to be God's dwelling place. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- James Smith: God's rest means perfect satisfaction in that which has been accomplished. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-commentary-james-smith
- **Where views differ (Sabbath):** Guzik (Calvary Chapel, listed among your Pentecostal/charismatic sites) argues from Col 2:16–17 and Gal 4:9–11 that Christians have no legal Sabbath obligation, though they still need a day of rest. He quotes Adam Clarke (Methodist) that idling through the six work days is as blameworthy as working on the seventh. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/ I couldn't get a Reformed or Lutheran page on the Sabbath, so I can't present their side.

**v. 4**
- Guzik says this is the first use of "LORD" (Yahweh) in the Bible. He reads Genesis 2 as Adam's own view of creation, filling out chapter 1 rather than contradicting it. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- Yahweh always appears together with Elohim in this chapter, which shows the God who made the universe is the same Lord who cared for Adam. Geisler: the new divine name shows a different purpose, not a different author; In chapter 1, God is the Creator, whereas in chapter 2 He is the Communicator. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Geisler also notes that some take "day" here to cover the whole creation period, which old-earth readers use as evidence. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Ellicott: this second narrative is strongly anthropomorphic. Here He forms, and builds, and plants, and breathes into His work. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/genesis-2.html

**vv. 5–6**
- Guzik ties "no rain" to a vapor canopy created on Day 2, which produced heavy dew or ground fog instead of rain. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- Translations split between "mist" (ESV, KJV-type) and "springs" or ground water (NET, CSB). https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary

**v. 7**
- Ellicott: the life was a gift direct from God, not a product of the body or of evolution. The dust stresses how frail man is. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/genesis/2-7.htm
- Barnes: the Hebrew word for "breath" (neshamah) is used only of God or man, never of animals. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/genesis/2-7.html
- Matthew Henry: when Jesus breathed on the disciples (John 20:22), He showed He was the one who first breathed life into man. He that made the soul is alone able to new-make it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/genesis/2-7.html
- J.C. Ryle (Anglican), cited in the Preacher's Homiletical Commentary, applies the verse to the new birth: God must breathe new life into us too. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/phc/genesis-2.html
- **Where views differ (what "living soul" means):**
  - Gill (Baptist): the soul is immaterial and immortal, unlike the body. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/genesis/2-7.htm
  - Ellicott (Anglican): "soul" here contains no idea of a spiritual existence, since animals are also called this. What sets man apart is how God gave the breath. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/genesis-2.html
  - Calvin likewise takes the word as animal life. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/genesis-2.html
  - Guzik says Scripture speaks both ways: man *is* a soul and *has* a soul. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- **Older critical note:** one of the commentaries on Bible Hub compares a Babylonian myth (man made from earth mixed with Marduk's blood) and the Greek Prometheus story. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/genesis/2-7.htm

**vv. 8–9**
- Guzik: Eden was planted as the perfect home for Adam. The tree of life gave or sustained eternal life (compare Rev 2:7, 22:2). The tree of knowledge may mean Adam would know evil by experience, or that God would test good and evil in man. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- Trees "pleasing to the eye" show that He values these things (beauty and pleasure). https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-devotionals-today-in-the-word

**vv. 10–14**
- Guzik thinks Adam may have written this as an eyewitness. He says the Flood erased the original rivers, and Noah's family later reused the names. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- A source quoted by Precept Austin warns it is risky to place Eden more exactly than the headwaters of the Tigris and Euphrates rivers in the highlands of Armenia. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Kingcomments reads bdellium as recalling manna, and so Christ the bread of life. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/kng/genesis-2.html

**v. 15**
- Work came before the Fall, so it is not a curse. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary and https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- The NET renders "garden" as "orchard." https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary

**vv. 16–17**
- Traditional reading: Adam had only one way to sin, and the command was given to him before Eve was made. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- Hodge: the tree was the outward and visible test of whether Adam would obey God in everything. In the day in which Adam ate the forbidden fruit he did die. https://www.monergism.com/covenant-works-2
- **Where views differ (covenant of works):**
  - Reformed: Ligonier says Perfect obedience to this covenant would have confirmed Adam and Eve in life. https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/what-is-the-covenant-of-works
  - TGC says the word "covenant" isn't in the text, but its elements are, and Hosea 6:7 most likely refers to this covenant with Adam. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/essay/jesus-christ-last-adam/
  - A bible.org article defends the doctrine and notes Berkhof's admission that "Scripture contains no explicit promise of eternal life to Adam." https://bible.org/article/does-genesis-215-17-teach-covenant-works
  - Dissent within the Reformed camp: John Murray says the name is not felicitous because it leaves out the element of grace, and the arrangement is not designated a covenant in Scripture. https://www.monergism.com/adamic-administration-john-murray
  - Guzik frames the tree mainly as a matter of free will: God wants love and obedience that is chosen. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- **Did Adam already know good and evil?**
  - William Kelly (Brethren): man had no knowledge of right and wrong as such until the Fall. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/genesis/2-7.html
  - Ligonier: Adam and Eve already had a basic knowledge, and the temptation was to become independent of God. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/covenant-works-part

**v. 18**
- First "not good" in the Bible; marriage belongs to God's design before sin. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- **Where emphases differ (what "helper" implies):**
  - Guzik reads the creation order and the word "helper" as making Adam head of the family. He limits male leadership to the home and the church. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
  - GotQuestions: She was not a subordinate but a complement. https://www.gotquestions.org/she-shall-be-called-woman.html

**vv. 19–20**
- No contradiction with chapter 1: the animals had already been formed. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Guzik: Adam, with his mind not yet damaged by the Fall, was brilliant. By not calling any animal "man," he showed he alone bore God's image. Naming the animals prepared him to receive the woman. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/

**vv. 21–22**
- Ellicott: the Hebrew word is translated "rib" only here; elsewhere it means "side." https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ebc/genesis-2.html
- Ellicott on v. 22: "made" is literally "built," which suggests care and skill. https://biblehub.com/genesis/2-22.htm
- Calvin: Adam lost a rib but gained a faithful companion, and through her he became complete. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/genesis-2.html
- Gill: Adam had thirteen ribs on a side (StudyLight's editor adds a note disagreeing). https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/genesis-2.html
- Matthew Henry: Eve came from Adam's side, not made out of his head to rule over him, nor out of his feet to be trampled upon. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/genesis/2-22.html
- Typology: Henry, Gill and Coffman see the Church formed from Christ's pierced side during His "sleep" of death. Coffman reads the blood and water as the two ordinances. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/genesis/2-22.html Guzik makes the same link. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/
- **Henry and Guzik on submission:** Henry applies the creation order to wives' submission. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/genesis/2-22.html Guzik says wives' subordination comes *before* the curse. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/genesis-2/

**v. 23**
- "Woman" (ishah) comes from "man" (ish). Naming the animals showed Adam's authority over them; naming the woman showed her likeness to him. https://www.gotquestions.org/she-shall-be-called-woman.html
- Calvin: God must have revealed to Adam how she was made. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/cal/genesis-2.html
- Ligonier: being taken from his side means she is equal in dignity. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/taken-out-man

**v. 24**
- Jesus goes back to this verse in Matthew 19 to show God's design for marriage. The new marriage takes priority over ties to parents. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- God's design is one man and one woman. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-devotionals-today-in-the-word

**v. 25**
- Adam and Eve were innocent, having no sin or guilt, and thus had no shame. https://www.preceptaustin.org/genesis-2-commentary
- Guzik: they knew they were physically naked, but had no sense of sinfulness or need to impress each other. https://es.enduringword.com/comentario-biblico/genesis-02/ (the English page was cut off before this verse, so this is from his Spanish edition)
